cards.title: Today’s vocabulary
sections: floor · /flɔr/ · noun · Meaning · New
A level of a building. Our room is on the second floor.
ramp · /ræmp/ · noun · Word · New
a sloping path connecting two different heights. There is a ramp beside the steps.
level · /ˈlɛvəl/ · noun · Word · New
a floor or height in a building. The cafe is on the same level as the entrance.
roof · /ruf/ · noun · Word · New
the outside covering on top of a building. The building has a flat roof.
ground floor · /ɡraʊnd flɔr/ · phrase · Phrase · New
The level of a building at ground level; usually called the first floor in American English. The front desk is on the ground floor.

articulation.label: first
articulation.alt: first: /f/ → /ɝ/ → /s/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /f/: Upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip.
/ɝ/: Bunch the tongue for American r; no tip contact.
/s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Read and write
sections: Reading

Heart enters an American hotel by a ramp beside the steps. The cafe is on the ground floor, the same level as the entrance. Here, the ground floor is also called the first floor. Her room is on the second floor. From its window, she can see the roof of a lower building.
Find the answer
Which level has the cafe and entrance?
Write
